title: Vertical position of the pitch-arm link hole relative to the hub A datum (millimetres)

provenance.branch_choices: Three of this chain's nodes are branch points and this study crosses all three having made a choice at each: at the hub A datum it takes the hub's own flange-to-flange dimension rather than either the blade-root or the ring-gear seat; at the hub top deck it takes the actuator mount rather than the tangential-link-mount or brake-mount seats; at the pitch plate connection it takes the pitch-link hole rather than the gas-spring bushing or the brake attachment. Those are engineering choices, made here by a human, and traverse() would have refused to make any of them.
provenance.note_on_values: Placeholder-heavy: two of the eight bands are `assumed` and the other six are untraced workbook cells. See the topology's provenance.

notes: The millimetre baseline for this topology, and the one that stops at the pitch arm ON PURPOSE: the pitch-arm coupling edge converts millimetres into degrees, so a millimetre chain ends at `pitch_link_arm_hole`, the interface just before it. Extending this selection across `pitch_arm_link_hole_to_clocking_hole` raises UnitMismatch, which is the correct answer and is pinned as such by tests/test_topology.py.
Every edge here runs downstream, so every sign is +1 and the total range is simply the sum of the bands. That makes it the readable case for checking the traversal by eye against the file.

This chain passes THROUGH the end stop: `end_stop_clearance` is the gap between the piston's travel-limiting face and the stop feature on the actuator body, and it enters the sum as an ordinary term because someone toleranced it.
